title: Theory of Space-Time, Vortical Motion and Geometry of Electromagnetism
content: By examining the theory of relativity as originally formulated by Lorentz and Poincaré, the fundamental relationship between Minkowski spacetime and matter can be established. This approach unifies relativity and electrodynamics while revealing an underlying non-Euclidean geometry. Consequently, a four-dimensional vortical theory of general motion, together with a corresponding vortex-based theory of interaction, is developed. Within this framework, the electromagnetic four-vector potential and field strength are interpreted respectively as velocity-like and vorticity-like fields in four dimensions. Moreover, the four-vector electric current density is shown to be proportional to the four-dimensional curvature vector of the potential field. This geometrical vortex formulation of electromagnetism captures its intrinsically vortical character, provides a geometrical and mechanical interpretation of the Lorentz force, and helps resolve existing ambiguities.
